payload.title: 15 Crete Wedding Venues From Elounda to Chania
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning 60 to 150 guests who will mostly fly in from Australia via Athens or a European hub. They have settled on Crete (or are weighing it against the Cyclades) and now need to choose between the east around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos, the central coast near Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania in the west, then shortlist venues compared on the same terms: ceremony options, capacity, rooms on site, exclusive use and how guests get there.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can check availability, ceremony options and house rules for the couple's shortlisted Crete venues on their dates and guest count, quoted in AUD.
payload.angle: Crete is big enough that the venue choice is really an area choice first: the airport you land at, the drive guests make and the style of the coast all change between Elounda in the east and Chania in the west. Most Crete lists mix every type of venue without saying where they sit or how guests reach them. This guide groups 15 venues by area, lists only venues whose own official site says they host weddings, and gives each the same fields in the same order (setting, ceremony options as the venue states them, capacity and rooms where published, exclusive use where offered, one standout detail). House rules a venue does not publish are written 'Not published' for the Wedded Advisor to confirm in writing. Around the venues sit an east versus west guide, getting there via Heraklion or Chania airport, when to marry, and the legal steps in brief from Australian Government sources.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: Crete's wedding areas (Elounda and Agios Nikolaos, the Heraklion coast, Rethymno, Chania and the west) and that the right one depends on guest count, ceremony type and which airport guests fly into; link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues prominently and the hub /destinations/europe/greece.
Crete wedding venues at a glance: a comparison table of the final list (area, type, ceremony options, capacity, rooms, exclusive use), with 'Not published' where a field is not published.
How to compare like for like: resort vs private villa with exclusive use vs estate or winery; ceremony type on site; seated capacity; rooms on site; nearest airport and transfer.
Choosing an area (east vs west Crete) as practical guidance: airport, guest travel, setting; no unsourced distances or drive times.

15 venues grouped by area, each verified on its own official site as hosting weddings, same fields in the same order; Elounda Beach Hotel & Villas and Nana Princess re-checked live with fresh wording. House rules not published written 'Not published' with one line per section that the Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing, and added to a booking checklist. Swap unconfirmable candidates from the reserves; do not pad (if fewer than 15 qualify, the title count changes and the person is told). No prices.
Getting there: Heraklion and Chania airports and transfers from official airport or tourism sources (visitgreece.gr, incrediblecrete.gr); Smartraveller Greece checked live (wildfire and heat season).
When to marry: season only as an official, tourism or venue source states it (Nana Princess ceremony-time guidance, fact_611, re-checked).

Legal in brief: civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies from Embassy Athens and Smartraveller facts in the greek-wedding-traditions and greece-wedding-venues source packs, re-checked; link the Greece venues guide's legal section; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once.

FAQ (4 to 6): Which part of Crete is best for a wedding? Can we book a venue for exclusive use? Which airport should guests fly into? When is the best time to marry in Crete? Can Australians legally marry in Crete?

Closing route to Wedded Concierge (/wonderland-concierge) with brand-facts claims only, invitation after the at-a-glance table and at the close; /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing.
avoid: Any price, fee or amount; any capacity, room count, distance or time not on an official source.
Phaea Blue and Domes of Elounda unless a weddings page is found.
Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find or confirm, sources, method, 'you will often read', myths sections); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once.
Ranking as 'best' in the copy; order by area with a stated logic (east to west).
Competitor wedding sites, directories, vendor blogs, review sites, Facebook groups or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.
Vendor names other than venues; venue contact details; implying partnerships or preferred rates.
Wedded Privileges or inclusions beyond brand-facts.md; 'from first idea to the last dance', 'last dance'.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords in brackets or pasted keywords in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue or destination.
